3.speaker: Narrator
3.text: I was having my afternoon tea in the state house office in Deyr and going through newspapers.

4.speaker: Narrator
4.text: One of the headlines piqued my interest. It read 'Polio Crisis in Wehlen'.

5.speaker: Narrator
5.text: Before I could start reading, I heard a couple of knocks. Paskal entered followed by Lucian.

6.speaker: Lucian Galade
6.text: “Mr. President. It's time for the scheduled healthcare meeting.”

11.speaker: Narrator
11.text: They have taken their seats and Paskal produced documents from his suitcase. He put them on the table.

12.speaker: Narrator
12.text: Paskal looked at the newspaper I was reading.

13.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
13.text: “Very troubling news from Wehlen, Mr. President.”

14.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
14.text: “I have just returned from a meeting with our top scientists on the matter of Polio. It seems to be spreading.”

15.speaker: Player
15.text: “Indeed. This might have dire consequences in the region.”

16.speaker: Player
16.text: “I'm not worried. It will stop before it reaches Sordland.”

17.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
17.text: “What I was told by our researchers was that with the current infection rate there will soon be millions of people affected by Polio.”

19.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
19.text: “We need to be ready for any possibility.”

20.speaker: Lucian Galade
20.text: “I doubt it is that serious yet.”

21.speaker: Lucian Galade
21.text: “Regardless, back to the topic. Mr. Beniwoll.”

24.speaker: Narrator
24.text: Paskal put on his reading glasses and went through the documents. He didn't say anything for a whole minute.

25.speaker: Narrator
25.text: He put the papers down, cleared his throat and looked at me.

29.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
29.text: “As you know, I have been preparing a new privatization program that would create funds through selling of unused ministry property and some extra taxes.”

30.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
30.text: “The overall mood has been positive as the administration focuses more on the healthcare. I'm excited about what we can achieve with the allocated funds.”

31.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
31.text: “The reduction of health funds is going to hurt no matter how we manage it. I will need to make big concessions, which will hamper our efforts.”

35.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
35.text: “But I'm still happy that the administration continues to support healthcare at the same level as before. Though, this limits our options significantly.”

36.speaker: Player
36.text: “We will have to make do with what we have. I want you to lead the way to solutions in healthcare.”

37.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
37.text: “I don't think that this is a matter that can be easily solved. More thought needs to be put in how do we go about lowering our budget or where do we cut it from.”

38.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
38.text: “I'm personally invested to solve the horrible infant and maternal death rates along with your requests.”

39.speaker: Player
39.text: “I'm sure you can figure out a way to come out of this strong. I have put trust in you.”

40.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
40.text: “I don't see many ways out of this particular situation. We need funds to bring improvements.”

41.speaker: Player
41.text: “Our health services seem to be working fine and don't require more investment. I'm sure we can improve what we have.”

42.speaker: Player
42.text: “Healthcare isn't a urgency for this administration. We have to make do with less.”

43.speaker: Player
43.text: “We have to minimize service disparity in the country. The situation isn't good at all.”

44.speaker: Player
44.text: “Providing better healthcare is our goal. This administration will be known to have supported the welfare services.”

45.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
45.text: “In general, I am very content with the budget decision that was made.”

46.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
46.text: “In general, the ministry is somewhat content with the budget decision that was made. At least we didn't get a cut.”

47.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
47.text: “In general, the ministry is not very content with the decision to cut the budget of our healthcare system.”

51.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
51.text: “This comes as no surprise as I know you are a man of your word. ”

52.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
52.text: “This comes as a very pleasant surprise that we all welcomed at the ministry.”

53.speaker: Player
53.text: “Do you have any specific areas of focus in mind?”

57.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
57.text: “Although, I have to say this came as a surprise to many since one of our campaign focuses was healthcare. I am not sure if we're abiding by that promise.”

61.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
61.text: “Although, I have to say this came as a surprise to many since one of our campaign focuses was healthcare. I am not sure if we're abiding by that promise.”

64.speaker: Lucian Galade
64.text: “I know of this too, Paskal. But this goes against our economic doctrine. Additionally, health is a key sector people expect to have in public hands.”

68.speaker: Lucian Galade
68.text: “It might not go against our strategy to promote a market economy, but I'm personally against privatization of government services. Such vital services must be under state control.”

69.speaker: Lucian Galade
69.text: “Aside from creating additional funds, there is a long-term problem with privatization in a country like Sordland.”

70.speaker: Lucian Galade
70.text: “Messing with that structure will definitely hurt us politically in the future. That I know for sure.”

71.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
71.text: “The market should take care of it by itself. We can't regulate people like that.”

72.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
72.text: “I do agree that there is some concern there... But the benefits of competitive and quality services is greater.”

73.speaker: Player
73.text: “You are right. There might be structural issues... Especially due to private greed and market manipulation.”

74.speaker: Player
74.text: “I don't see a problem with privatization. It would create additional funds and boost enterprise.”

75.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
75.text: “We will prevent the worst case scenarios. There needs to be healthy structural improvements in this sector.”

76.speaker: Lucian Galade
76.text: “Also in a country where most people don't have access to quality healthcare...”

77.speaker: Lucian Galade
77.text: “People are already lacking proper healthcare even though it is free. What happens when you privatise? Prices increase as state hospitals close due to sales.”

78.speaker: Lucian Galade
78.text: “For now it wouldn't. Privatization would be fair if our healthcare standards were high and accessible for all.”

80.speaker: Lucian Galade
80.text: “This is not Arcasia nor Lespia. You are talking about Sordland, in which the healthcare is free for now.”

81.speaker: Lucian Galade
81.text: “We have people who have their lives depending on a service that is free to them.”

82.speaker: Lucian Galade
82.text: “But the choice is yours, Mr. President.”

84.speaker: Player
84.text: “We'll keep healthcare in state control. Don't allow any private involvement that could endanger core health services.”

85.speaker: Lucian Galade
85.text: "It's largely due to outdated facilities that lack proper hygiene standards and equipment."

86.speaker: Player
86.text: “Building new hospitals sounds interesting. It would also boost our popularity.”

92.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
92.text: “Excellent. We can turn that extra money to something useful. I shall let my partners know.”

93.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
93.text: “As you wish. The health services shall remain in public hands.”

101.speaker: Lucian Galade
101.text: “I don't think this was the right choice.”

103.speaker: Lucian Galade
103.text: “Very well. Fruitful meeting nevertheless. Nice and short.”

105.speaker: Player
105.text: “Improve rural treatment by hiring health staff and upgrading equipment in rural areas.”

106.speaker: Player
106.text: “Increase salaries of doctors, nurses and other health staff with incentives for rural areas.”

107.speaker: Player
107.text: “Build new hospitals where they are needed. Access to health will be available for all.”

108.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
108.text: “Since we will have extra funds, the spending policy question remains.”
108.conditionsRaw: ((Variable["BaseGame.Turn03_EnT_Healthcare_Budget_Increase"] == true) == false) and (Variable["BaseGame.Turn03_EnT_Healthcare_Budget_Maintain"] == true  and  Variable["BaseGame.Turn06_PSnW_Healthcare_Privatization"] == true)

110.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
110.text: “Now let's get to the big question of how we will spend the extra funds dedicated to the Ministry of Health.”

120.speaker: Narrator
120.text: Paskal gathered his documents and left along with Lucian.

127.speaker: Lucian Galade
127.text: "It's a visible, tangible improvement that we can present as our achievement."

128.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
128.text: "The sad reality is that our rural clinics are woefully outdated, ill-equipped, and understaffed."

129.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
129.text: “We can initiate one more spending policy with our funds. Which one would should we initiate?”

130.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
130.text: “I urge you to consider these proposals. We could build new hospitals where necessary, divert funds to increase the salaries of our health workers, or invest in enhancing the existing treatment facilities in rural areas.”

131.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
131.text: "While the construction of new hospitals is an appealing idea, I personally don't see it as a primary concern."

132.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
132.text: “Each of these options presents a unique path towards improving healthcare access and quality in Sordland.”

133.speaker: Lucian Galade
133.text: "However, implementing a nationwide, proportional salary boost would pay off politically."

134.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
134.text: “Therefore, I believe improving treatment in rural areas should be our course of action, Mr. President.”

135.speaker: Narrator
135.text: A few minutes went by in contemplation as the moment to make a decision came near.

136.speaker: Player
136.text: “Increasing salaries should have a good effect for doctors, nurses and other staff who work so hard for our citizens.”

137.speaker: Player
137.text: “Improving treatment in rural areas is a must. It would prevent mistreatment, disease and sickness.”

138.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
138.text: "Well, that wraps up our discussion for now."
138.conditionsRaw: ((Variable["BaseGame.Turn03_EnT_Healthcare_Budget_Increase"] == true) == false) and ((Variable["BaseGame.Turn03_EnT_Healthcare_Budget_Maintain"] == true  and  Variable["BaseGame.Turn06_PSnW_Healthcare_Privatization"] == true) == false) and ((Variable["BaseGame.Turn03_EnT_Healthcare_Budget_Increase"] == true  and  Variable["BaseGame.Turn06_PSnW_Healthcare_Privatization"] == true) == false) and (Variable["BaseGame.Promise_TermFocus_Health"] == true) and ((Variable["BaseGame.Promise_TermFocus_Health"] == true) == false)

139.speaker: Lucian Galade
139.text: “It would be best to consider the political advantages of each one, as well as the practical advantages before making a decision.”

141.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
141.text: "There's merit in the proposal to increase salaries for all health staff, with an extra emphasis on rural areas."

147.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
147.text: “New contracts for improvements will be drawn up immediately.”

149.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
149.text: "In my view, the pressing issue lies in the quality and accessibility of healthcare in remote areas."

150.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
150.text: "This approach could incentivize doctors and nurses to work in these regions where their services are desperately needed."

151.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
151.text: "This stark disparity between urban and rural healthcare is a major contributor to the high maternal mortality rates and prevalence of other diseases in our rural communities."

152.speaker: Lucian Galade
152.text: "Constructing new hospitals would score us significant political points."

153.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
153.text: “I'll prepare the increase as soon as possible. The workers will rejoice.”

154.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
154.text: “We shall begin plans of hospital constructions immediately.”

155.speaker: Lucian Galade
155.text: "Metropolitan areas are already reaping the benefits of our policies. The rural regions, which trail behind in income, deserve some attention."

156.speaker: Lucian Galade
156.text: "We're seeing an uptick in minor outbreaks in specific regions."

159.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
159.text: “So we have notified all of our healthcare staff especially the ones closer to the Wehlen border. Unfortunately these are also the more rural areas where we lack equipment and staff.”

160.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
160.text: “We have notified all of our healthcare staff, especially the ones closer to the Wehlen border. Unfortunately, these are also the more rural areas where we lack equipment and staff.”

161.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
161.text: “What I was told by our researchers was that with the current infection rate, there will soon be millions of people affected by Polio.”

166.speaker: Player
166.text: “Why am I just learning this from a newspaper?”

167.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
167.text: “We are already evaluating the situation and did not want to bother you with it yet, Mr. President. We are working on a comprehensive report.”

168.speaker: Player
168.text: “It was not a decision that I made lightly.”

169.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
169.text: “I am sure, Mr. President. I am not questioning that. But...”

170.speaker: Player
170.text: “It was not a decision that I made lightly.”

171.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
171.text: “I am sure, Mr. President. I am not questioning that. But...”

172.speaker: Player
172.text: “Build new hospitals where they are needed. Access to health will be available for all.”

174.speaker: Player
174.text: “Improve rural treatment by hiring health staff and upgrading equipment in rural areas.”

175.speaker: Player
175.text: “Increase salaries of doctors, nurses and other health staff with incentives for rural areas.”

191.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
191.text: “I'll prepare the increase as soon as possible. The workers will rejoice.”

192.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
192.text: “We shall begin plans of hospital constructions immediately.”

193.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
193.text: “New contracts for improvements will be drawn up immediately.”

259.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
259.text: "In my book 'The Unfortunate Man', I depicted the hardships of a poor mining family, a vivid illustration of the stark health inequalities in our society."

260.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
260.text: "As Minister of Health, I strive to rectify these disparities."

274.speaker: Player
274.text: “We can proceed with the decision, Minister Beniwoll.”

277.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
277.conditionsRaw: (Variable["BaseGameIsolated.HealthBudget_Hub_Option1"] == true  or Variable["BaseGameIsolated.HealthBudget_Hub_Option2"] == true  or Variable["BaseGameIsolated.HealthBudget_Hub_Option3"] == true) == false

278.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
278.text: "But certainly, adding new healthcare facilities would be a positive step, particularly in underserved regions."

279.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
279.text: "On a larger scale, it would boost satisfaction within the health industry and could contribute significantly to reducing maternal mortality rates, a goal that is close to my heart."

280.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
280.text: "Addressing this issue is one of my key objectives in this term, and I believe an overhaul of the rural healthcare infrastructure is a critical step in that direction."

282.speaker: Player
282.text: “We will promote privatization and allow the private sector to invest and buy government's health properties.” [+2 Government Budget]

287.speaker: Player
287.text: “We will promote privatization and allow the private sector to invest and buy government's health properties.” [+1 Government Budget]
